subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Should this issue stay as the canonical maintainer-owned live-reproduction task for the remaining healthy local vLLM false-timeout and gateway RPC latency symptoms, or should the remaining symptoms be split into narrower owner-boundary issues first?
rationale: Current source proves partial fixes but not the full reported cascade; choosing the fix layer without a live trace could change provider timeout, fallback, auth-profile, cron, or gateway behavior in the wrong place.

options.title: Capture canonical live trace first
options.body: Keep this issue open and gather current-main vLLM timing, fallback, auth, cron/live-session, and gateway RPC evidence before choosing the fix layer.

options.title: Split remaining symptoms
options.body: Create narrower follow-up issues for provider timeout, gateway RPC backpressure, and cron/live-session interactions, then use this issue as the umbrella reference.

options.title: Attempt a code fix now
options.body: Let a contributor target the most likely timeout/fallback path from source inspection, accepting higher risk that the patch addresses the wrong layer.

recommendation.title: Capture canonical live trace first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and gather current-main vLLM timing, fallback, auth, cron/live-session, and gateway RPC evidence before choosing the fix layer.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz and the adjacent cron fallback fix was merged by osolmaz, making them the best available routing owner for the next maintainer decision.
